summary.title: SPOT-Contact-Single: Improving Single-Sequence-Based Prediction of Protein Contact Map using a Transformer Language Model
summary.authors: Jaspreet Singh; Thomas Litfin; Jaswinder Singh; Kuldip Paliwal; Yaoqi Zhou
summary.executive_summary: This study introduces SPOT-Contact-Single, a novel protein contact map predictor designed to operate without evolutionary information, addressing the limitations of existing methods that rely on Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSA) which are unavailable for many proteins. The authors developed an ensemble of ResNet architectures that integrate one-hot encoded amino acid sequences, structural features from SPOT-1D-Single, and attention maps from the pre-trained ESM-1b Transformer language model. By leveraging unsupervised learning features from ESM-1b, the method achieves significant performance gains over single-sequence baselines like SSCpred and evolutionary-profile-based methods like TrRosetta and SPOT-Contact, particularly for proteins with low effective number of homologs (Neff). The proposed approach offers a computationally efficient alternative, being orders of magnitude faster than MSA-dependent methods, making it suitable for large-scale genomic predictions where homologous sequences are scarce or generation is computationally prohibitive.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study introduces SPOT-Contact-Single, a novel protein contact map predictor designed to operate without evolutionary information, addressing the limitations of existing methods that rely on Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSA) which are unavailable for many proteins. The authors developed an ensemble of ResNet architectures that integrate one-hot encoded amino acid sequences, structural features from SPOT-1D-Single, and attention maps from the pre-trained ESM-1b Transformer language model. By leveraging unsupervised learning features from ESM-1b, the method achieves significant performance gains over single-sequence baselines like SSCpred and evolutionary-profile-based methods like TrRosetta and SPOT-Contact, particularly for proteins with low effective number of homologs (Neff). The proposed approach offers a computationally efficient alternative, being orders of magnitude faster than MSA-dependent methods, making it suitable for large-scale genomic predictions where homologous sequences are scarce or generation is computationally prohibitive.

Research Context
Protein contact maps are essential for structure and function prediction. Most existing methods rely on protein-sequence-evolutionary information. Evolutionary profiles may not exist due to lack of homologous sequences. Generating evolutionary profiles is computationally intensive. Single-sequence methods provide less information for learning.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can unsupervised language model features improve single-sequence prediction? Will this method outperform MSA-based predictors for low Neff proteins? Does an ensemble of models with different feature combinations add value? Is the method faster than evolution-based alternatives?

Methodological Details
The study utilized the benchmark dataset prepared by ProteinNet. The dataset consists of 50914 proteins submitted to PDB before 2016. Proteins were clustered at sequence identity cut-off at 95%. 100 proteins were separated for validation to minimize over-fitting. Proteins with hits at e-value cut-off of less than 0.1 were removed. The final training set contains 34691 proteins. The final validation set contains 88 proteins. The stringent test set SPOT-2018 contains 669 proteins. The Neff1-2018 test set contains 46 proteins with Neff=1. The CASP14-FM test set includes 15 free modelling targets. Features included one-hot encoding, SPOT-1D-Single outputs, and ESM-1b attention maps. Attention maps were gathered using all twenty attention heads. Maps were symmetrized and applied average product corrections.

Procedures And Architectures
The architecture was inspired by the success of the ResNet architecture. A 12 block ResNet was used as the maximum depth. Convolutional layers had a channel size of 64 and kernel size of 3. Six models were trained with different input feature combinations. The first three models predicted inter-residue contacts as binary classification. The last three models predicted inter-residue distances as distance bins. Direct models used Binary Cross-Entropy loss. Distogram models used Cross-Entropy loss. The Adam optimizer was used with a learning rate of 0.001. A batch size of 1 was used for training. Early stopping of 3 was applied to avoid overfitting. The ensemble results were obtained by taking the mean of individual models.

Key Results
SPOT-Contact-Single showed 15% improvement in F1-score over SSCpred. Improvement over SSCpred was 15% on the CASP14-FM test set. Improvement over TrRosetta was 48.7% on proteins without homologs. Improvement over SPOT-Contact was 48.5% on proteins without homologs. The improvement was observed on proteins without homologs (Neff=1). The method is 22 times faster than TrRosetta on CPU. The method is 42 times faster than TrRosetta on GPU. The ensemble achieved 4% improvement over the second-best individual model. F1-score for SPOT-Contact-Single on Neff1-2018 was 0.388. F1-score for TrRosetta on Neff1-2018 was 0.252. F1-score for ESM-1b on Neff1-2018 was 0.235. F1-score for SPOT-Contact on Neff1-2018 was 0.215. One-hot encoding alone achieved an F1-score of 0.15. Adding SPOT-1D-Single improved F1-score by 22.90%. Attention maps from last layer led to F1 of 0.51. Result was 242% improvement in F1-score over one-hot encoding. Concatenating all features increased F1-score by 2.92%. Long-range contacts precision improved by ~100% over SSCpred.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Unsupervised learning features concatenated with one-hot encoding outperform single-sequence methods. Multiple sequence alignment provides co-mutation information more effectively. The method serves as a reasonably accurate screening tool for low Neff proteins. The method is suitable for genomic scale prediction due to speed. Further improvement may come from using Transformer or Performer architectures.

Contradictions And Limitations
The method cannot directly predict contact maps for proteins with more than 1024 amino acids. SPOT-1D-Single is not yet as competitive as evolution-based methods for high Neff. Performance of profile-based predictors improves over SPOT-1D-Single as Neff increases. The study relied on a specific version of ResNet which may limit generalizability.

Claims
SPOT-Contact-Single significantly outperforms single-sequence and evolutionary methods for proteins without homologs. 15% improvement in F1-score over SSCpred. 48.7% improvement over TrRosetta on Neff=1 proteins. F1-score of 0.388 vs 0.252 for TrRosetta on Neff1-2018. Profile-based methods are more competitive as Neff increases. The method is useful for large-scale prediction where homologs are scarce.
The method is computationally efficient compared to evolutionary profile-based methods. 22 times faster than TrRosetta on CPU. 42 times faster than TrRosetta on GPU.  Sequence profile generation takes significantly longer than the proposed method.

Data And Code Availability
Stand-alone programs for TrRosetta, SPOT-Contact, and ESM-1b are available online. SSCpred web-server was utilized due to lack of stand-alone version.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Direct contact-map prediction performs slightly better than distogram-based prediction. Ensemble of six models gained 4% improvement over the second-best individual model. Attention maps from all layers showed continued improvement in precision.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is a single-sequence-based predictor using ESM-1b attention maps. 2. The strongest evidence is the 48.7% improvement over TrRosetta on Neff=1 proteins. 3. The future path involves using more advanced architectural models like Transformer.
